To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SmartSkeMAs, UAV, and ABE can potentially contribute to land administration in Kajiado, and other similar contexts.

SmartSkeMAs are a versatile and community responsive land data acquisition tool, requiring little expertise to use; UAVs are a high potential for up-to-date base map creation, able to support the existing land administration system; and automatic boundary extraction (using UAV images) is an effective method for demarcating physical and visible boundaries, compared to traditional methods and manual delineation.

SmartSkeMAs can support the collection of land data in a community-driven and participatory manner, UAVs can be used to collect data to create up-to-date base-maps, which are needed to support the land administration system in Kenya, and ABE techniques are effective methods to demarcate land tenure boundaries.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing innovative and cost-effective methods for mapping land tenure in Kenya and other similar developing countries.
the development of a land tenure mapping approach that can be implemented at the national scale.
the development of a remote sensing methodology that can be applied to support land rights documentation and land administration in developing countries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the remote sensing methodologies developed, adapted, and tested in the context of this research have the potential to support the protection of land tenure rights and the development of a more inclusive land administration system in Kenya.
the three remote sensing methodologies have a potential to support land rights documentation in Kenya, and that the SmartSkeMa methodology was identified as the most promising.
the proposed methodologies are promising for land rights documentation and mapping.
